'''Zachary David Alexander Efron''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ɛ|f|r|ɒ|n}}; born October 18, 1987) is an American actor.<!-- Do not add other occupations unless they are notable per [[MOS:LEADSENTENCE]] --> Efron began acting professionally in the early 2000s and rose to prominence as a [[teen idol]] for his leading role as [[Troy Bolton]] in the [[High School Musical (franchise)|''High School Musical'' film series]] (2006–2008). During this time, he also starred in the musical film ''[[Hairspray (2007 film)|Hairspray]]'' (2007) and the comedy film ''[[17 Again (film)|17 Again]]'' (2009).

Efron had starring roles in ''[[New Year's Eve (2011 film)|New Year's Eve]]'' (2011), ''[[The Lucky One (film)|The Lucky One]]'' (2012), ''[[The Paperboy (2012 film)|The Paperboy]]'' (2012), ''[[Neighbors (2014 film)|Neighbors]]'' (2014), ''[[That Awkward Moment]]'' (2014) ''[[Dirty Grandpa]]'' (2016), ''[[Baywatch (film)|Baywatch]]'' (2017), and ''[[The Greatest Showman]]'' (2017). His roles have included [[Ted Bundy]] in ''[[Extremely Wicked, Shockingly Evil and Vile]]'' (2019) and [[Kevin Von Erich]] in ''[[The Iron Claw (film)|The Iron Claw]]'' (2023).

In 2021, he won a [[Daytime Emmy Awards|Daytime Emmy Award]] for hosting the [[Netflix]] travel show ''[[Down to Earth with Zac Efron]]'' (2020–2022). In 2023, he received [[List of actors with Hollywood Walk of Fame motion picture stars|a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://walkoffame.com/zac-efron/|title=Zac Efron|work=walkoffame.com}}</ref>

==Career==

=== 2002–2009: Early career and ''High School Musical'' ===
[[File:Zac Efron 2007.jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|Efron at the [[Nickelodeon Australian Kids' Choice Awards 2007|2007 Nickelodeon Australian Kids' Choice Awards]]]]
Efron began acting in the early 2000s with guest roles on several television series including ''[[Firefly (TV series)|Firefly]]'',<ref>{{cite web |date=March 13, 2011 |title=Before The Fame: Zac Efron In Cute Guest Appearance! |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/zac-efron-in-firefly_n_835018 |access-date=September 4, 2019 |website=HuffPost |archive-date=October 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231014092929/https://www.huffpost.com/entry/zac-efron-in-firefly_n_835018 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[ER (TV series)|ER]]'', and ''[[The Guardian (TV series)|The Guardian]]''. In 2004, he began appearing as a recurring character in the first season of the [[The WB Television Network|WB]] series ''[[Summerland (TV series)|Summerland]]''.<ref name="Boren">{{cite web |last=Boren |first=Jade |date=April 30, 2019 |title=Zac Efron Confesses He Ruined His First On-Screen Kiss In A Really Gross Way — Watch |url=https://hollywoodlife.com/2019/04/30/zac-efron-first-onscreen-kiss-seafood-summerland-kay-panabaker-interview/ |access-date=September 4, 2019 |website=Hollywood Life |archive-date=October 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231014092321/https://hollywoodlife.com/2019/04/30/zac-efron-first-onscreen-kiss-seafood-summerland-kay-panabaker-interview/ |url-status=live }}</ref> For the show's second season, which aired in 2005, he was promoted to the main cast. He also appeared in some films, including the [[Lifetime (TV network)|Lifetime]] television film ''[[Miracle Run]]'' (2004), for which he earned a [[Young Artist Award]] nomination for his performance as one of two autistic twins.

Efron's career reached a turning point with the teen musical television film ''[[High School Musical]]'' (2006), which premiered on the [[Disney Channel]] in January 2006. The film, which has been described as a modern adaptation of ''[[Romeo and Juliet]]'',{{by whom|date=February 2026}} saw Efron playing the male lead Troy Bolton, a high school basketball player who feels conflicted when he finds himself interested in participating in the school musical with Gabriella Montez ([[Vanessa Hudgens]]), a girl from the scholastic decathlon team. The film's success helped Efron gain recognition among teenage audiences. The film's soundtrack was certified quadruple platinum by the [[RIAA]].<ref>{{cite web |title=RIA Gold & Platinum |website=[[Recording Industry Association of America]] |url=http://riaa.com/goldandplatinum.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091231133408/http://riaa.com/goldandplatinum.php |archive-date=December 31, 2009 |access-date=December 17, 2008}}</ref>  However, Efron's recordings of the film's songs were not included in the final cut, and the majority of his parts were sung by [[Drew Seeley]];<ref>{{Cite web |last=Siwak |first=Miranda |date=August 27, 2021 |title=No Drama Here! Drew Seeley Doesn't Regret Voicing Troy Bolton In 'HSM' |url=https://www.usmagazine.com/entertainment/news/drew-seeley-doesnt-regret-high-school-musical-voiceover/ |access-date=October 12, 2022 |website=Us Weekly |language=en-US |archive-date=October 12, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221012140719/https://www.usmagazine.com/entertainment/news/drew-seeley-doesnt-regret-high-school-musical-voiceover/ |url-status=live }}</ref> the Troy Bolton role had been intended for a tenor before Efron's casting and Efron was a baritone. In his subsequent musical films, Efron did his own singing.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 22, 2017 |title=Just a Reminder That Zac Efron Wasn't Actually Singing in the First "HSM" |url=https://www.teenvogue.com/story/zac-efron-high-school-musical-voice |access-date=October 12, 2022 |website=Teen Vogue |language=en-US |archive-date=June 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220628173530/https://www.teenvogue.com/story/zac-efron-high-school-musical-voice |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Zac Efron 2008 (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Efron in 2008]]
Efron was next seen as Link Larkin in the musical comedy film ''[[Hairspray (2007 film)|Hairspray]]'' (2007), based on the [[Hairspray (musical)|2002 Broadway musical of the same name]]. Production conflicted with the [[High School Musical: The Concert|High School Musical concert tour]], which prevented Efron from joining; Drew Seeley filled in. The film became a major commercial and critical success upon its release in July 2007. Later that year, he reprised his role of Troy Bolton in ''[[High School Musical 2]]'' (2007), which aired on the Disney Channel in August 2007.

Efron again reprised his role in ''[[High School Musical 3: Senior Year]]'' (2008), the first film in the ''High School Musical'' franchise to receive a theatrical release. The film succeeded at the box office, and received mixed to positive reviews from critics. He followed this with the commercially successful comedy ''[[17 Again (film)|17 Again]]'' (2009) about a 37-year-old man who is transformed into his 17-year-old self (Efron) after a chance accident.

=== 2009–present: Dramatic roles and mainstream projects ===
[[File:Zac Efron Cannes 2012.jpg|thumb|Efron at the [[2012 Cannes Film Festival]]]]
Efron's next release was [[Richard Linklater]]'s period drama ''[[Me and Orson Welles]]'', which premiered at the [[2008 Toronto International Film Festival|Toronto International Film Festival]] in September 2008 and received a wide release in late 2009. The film earned mostly positive reviews from critics. He then played the title role in the supernatural romantic drama ''[[Charlie St. Cloud (film)|Charlie St. Cloud]]'' (2010), which became a moderate success at the box office despite receiving mostly negative reviews from critics. Efron appeared as a part of the large ensemble cast in [[Garry Marshall]]'s ''[[New Year's Eve (2011 film)|New Year's Eve]]'' (2011), which depicted a series of holiday vignettes of different groups of characters. The film received almost unanimously negative reviews from critics, but did well at the box office. He also played a supporting role in the critically successful ''[[Liberal Arts (film)|Liberal Arts]]'' (2012), which premiered at the [[2012 Sundance Film Festival|Sundance Film Festival]] in January 2012 and received a limited release later that year. He also starred in ''[[The Paperboy (2012 film)|The Paperboy]]'' (2012), which premiered at the [[2012 Cannes Film Festival|Cannes Film Festival]] in May 2012 and received a wider release later that year. The film received mixed to negative reviews from critics.

After lending his voice to the animated film ''[[The Lorax (film)|The Lorax]]'' (2012), he appeared as the male lead in the romantic drama ''[[The Lucky One (film)|The Lucky One]]'' (2012), based on the [[The Lucky One (novel)|novel of the same name]] by [[Nicholas Sparks]]. The film became a success financially despite negative reviews from critics. He also starred in the drama ''[[At Any Price (film)|At Any Price]]'', which premiered at the [[69th Venice International Film Festival|2012 Venice International Film Festival]], and the historical drama ''[[Parkland (film)|Parkland]]'', which premiered at the [[70th Venice International Film Festival|2013 Venice International Film Festival]]. Both films received mixed reviews from critics. Efron's first release of 2014 was the romantic comedy ''[[That Awkward Moment]]'', for which he also served as an executive producer. The film, which starred Efron as one of three bachelors in New York City, became a moderate commercial success despite receiving mostly negative reviews from critics.

[[File:Zac Efron - workout addict.jpg|thumb|left|Efron in 2012]]
Later in 2014, Efron was seen in the adult comedy ''[[Neighbors (2014 film)|Neighbors]]'' (2014). The film revolved around a young couple who struggle to raise their baby daughter while living next to the house of a wild fraternity led by its president, played by Efron. The film was a commercial success and earned mostly positive reviews from critics, who also added that he had successfully shed his "Disney pretty boy" image.<ref name="usatoday.com">{{cite web |last=Mandell |first=Andrea |date=May 6, 2014 |title=Zac Efron sends up his image in ''Neighbors'' |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/people/2014/05/06/zac-efron-sends-up-his-image-in-neighbors/8609967/ |access-date=January 27, 2015 |website=USA Today |archive-date=October 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231014093003/https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/people/2014/05/06/zac-efron-sends-up-his-image-in-neighbors/8609967/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Efron's only release in 2015 was the moderately successful ''[[We Are Your Friends (film)|We Are Your Friends]]'', in which he played a struggling DJ. In January 2016, he starred in the adult comedy ''[[Dirty Grandpa]]'' as a straitlaced young man who begrudgingly indulges his grandfather's unhinged personality by taking him on a vacation to Florida. The film received mostly negative reviews from critics for its crude humor but became a commercial success.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mediaweek |date=February 9, 2016 |title=Box Office Report: Dirty Grandpa keeps sleaze #1, Zoolander 2 previews miss second spot |url=https://www.mediaweek.com.au/12859-2/ |access-date=June 19, 2024 |website=Mediaweek |language=en-AU |quote=The second weekend of the Robert De Niro and Zac Efron sleaze-fest Dirty Grandpa has again defied the critics and maintained top spot at the box office.}}</ref> He subsequently starred in the comedy sequel ''[[Neighbors 2: Sorority Rising]]'', which became a commercial and critical success upon its release in May 2016. The film followed the same couple who team up with their former rival (Efron) to take down a hard-partying sorority led by a freshman. His third 2016 comedy, released in July, was ''[[Mike and Dave Need Wedding Dates]].''
[[File:Zac Efron in 2017.jpg|thumb|Efron in 2017]]

Also in 2017, Efron had a supporting role in two biographical films released in December: ''[[The Disaster Artist (film)|The Disaster Artist]]'', a comedy-drama directed by and starring [[James Franco]], and as Phillip in the musical ''[[The Greatest Showman]]''. === Health ===
Efron sought treatment in early 2013 after struggling with [[alcoholism]] and [[substance abuse]]. He got sober in June 2013.<ref name="usatoday.com" /> In November 2013, Efron had to have his [[Jaw wiring|jaw wired shut]] after an injury from a fall at home.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 31, 2014 |title=Zac Efron Broke Jaw on Home Fountain, Lost "10–12 Pounds" Drinking Liquid Foods For Six Weeks |url=http://www.usmagazine.com/celebrity-news/news/zac-efron-broke-jaw-on-home-fountain-lost-10-12-pounds-drinking-liquid-foods-for-six-weeks-2014311 |access-date=September 7, 2015 |website=[[Us Weekly]] |archive-date=March 28, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328202549/https://www.usmagazine.com/celebrity-news/news/zac-efron-broke-jaw-on-home-fountain-lost-10-12-pounds-drinking-liquid-foods-for-six-weeks-2014311/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He revealed in 2022 that he almost died during this incident, and that it was responsible for his facial swelling, apparent in a viral 2021 video for [[Bill Nye]]'s Earth Day Musical.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zac Efron says he 'almost died' in the severe accident that shattered his jaw and led people to speculate he'd had plastic surgery |url=https://www.insider.com/zac-efron-debunks-plastic-surgery-before-after-jaw-injury-2022-9 |website=Insider |access-date=February 13, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Zac Efron Finally Explains Why His Jaw Looked So Huge |url=https://www.menshealth.com/entertainment/a41093855/zac-efron-jaw/ |website=Men's Health |date=September 7, 2022 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |archive-date=October 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221027085452/https://www.menshealth.com/entertainment/a41093855/zac-efron-jaw/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Zachary David Alexander Efron (; born October 18, 1987) is an American actor. Efron began acting professionally in the early 2000s and rose to prominence as a teen idol for his leading role as Troy Bolton in the High School Musical film series (2006–2008). During this time, he also starred in the musical film Hairspray (2007) and the comedy film 17 Again (2009).
Efron had starring roles in New Year's Eve (2011), The Lucky One (2012), The Paperboy (2012), Neighbors (2014), That Awkward Moment (2014) Dirty Grandpa (2016), Baywatch (2017), and The Greatest Showman (2017). His roles have included Ted Bundy in Extremely Wicked, Shockingly Evil and Vile (2019) and Kevin Von Erich in The Iron Claw (2023).
In 2021, he won a Daytime Emmy Award for hosting the Netflix travel show Down to Earth with Zac Efron (2020–2022). In 2023, he received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.
